question: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1951 was awarded jointly to Edwin Mattison McMillan and ______ for their discoveries in the chemistry of the transuranium elements
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glenn T Seaborg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1951 was awarded jointly to Edwin Mattison McMillan and Glenn T. Seaborg "for their discoveries in the chemistry of the transuranium elements". (रसायन विज्ञान में नोबेल पुरस्कार 1951 — ग्लेन टी. सीबॉर्ग)

 

• Seaborg led the team that discovered several transuranium elements, including plutonium (Pu), americium, curium, berkelium, californium, einsteinium, fermium, mendelevium and nobelium.

 

• McMillan discovered neptunium (Np), the first transuranium element, in 1940, along with Philip Abelson.

 

• Element 106 was later named Seaborgium (Sg) in his honour — one of the very few elements named after a living person at the time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Transuranium (or transuranic) elements are elements with atomic number greater than 92 (uranium), most of which are synthetic and radioactive.

 

• McMillan and Seaborg's joint work at the University of California, Berkeley, laid the foundation for the modern actinide series of the periodic table.

 

NOTE

 

• Jacob Berzelius (Option 1): A 19th-century Swedish chemist, considered one of the founders of modern chemistry; he had no connection with this 1951 award.

 

• Leon Jouhaux (Option 2): A French trade unionist who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1951, not the Chemistry prize.

 

• Albert Schweitzer (Option 4): A theologian-physician who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1952, unrelated to Chemistry 1951.

question: The folk dance Hojagiri originated and is associated with which part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North-East.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hojagiri is a traditional folk dance of the Reang (Bru) tribe of Tripura, a state in North-East India. (होजागिरी नृत्य — त्रिपुरा, पूर्वोत्तर भारत)

 

• It is performed by young women who balance on top of an earthen pitcher (ghara) while balancing a bottle on the head and an earthen lamp on the hands, dancing to the accompaniment of traditional instruments like sumui (flute), do-tara and sarinda.

 

• The dance is performed during the Hojagiri festival, dedicated to the goddess Mailuma (a form of Goddess Lakshmi), usually around the harvest season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk dances of Tripura include Garia, Lebang Boomani and Wangala-linked dances of neighbouring communities.

 

• Tripura is one of the Seven Sister States of North-East India, bordering Bangladesh.

 

NOTE

 

• South (Option 1): Southern folk dances include Bharatanatyam-linked forms, Kolattam, and others — none associated with Hojagiri.

 

• North (Option 3): Northern India is home to dances like Bhangra and Ghoomar, unrelated to Hojagiri.

 

• West (Option 4): Western India is known for Garba and Dandiya Raas, not Hojagiri.

question: Which of the following states has maximum literacy rate according to census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Kerala recorded India's highest literacy rate (93.91%), but among the states listed in this question, Mizoram has the highest literacy rate at about 91.58%. (जनगणना 2011 साक्षरता दर — मिज़ोरम)

 

• Mizoram consistently ranks among the top literacy-rate states in the country, just behind Kerala and Lakshadweep (a Union Territory).

 

• In comparison, Rajasthan (~66.11%), Arunachal Pradesh (~65.38%) and Bihar (~61.80%) all recorded much lower literacy rates in Census 2011, with Bihar having the lowest literacy rate among all Indian states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census 2011 was India's 15th national census; the next census was due in 2021 but was postponed.

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (82.14% for males, 65.46% for females).

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 2): Had a moderate literacy rate (~65.38%), well below Mizoram's.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Had a literacy rate of about 66.11%, higher than Bihar but far below Mizoram.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Recorded the lowest literacy rate among Indian states in Census 2011.

question: In hockey, what is the meaning if the umpire signals by pointing both arms horizontally toward the centre of the field?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goal scored.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In field hockey, when the umpire points both arms horizontally toward the centre of the field, it signals that a goal has been scored. (हॉकी अंपायर संकेत — गोल स्कोर)

 

• After signalling a goal, play is restarted with a pass-back from the centre of the field by the team that conceded the goal.

 

• Umpire hand signals in hockey are standardised by the International Hockey Federation (FIH) so that players, officials and spectators can identify decisions instantly without verbal announcement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A penalty corner is signalled by the umpire raising one arm with the hand bent at a right angle at the elbow, and pointing towards the 23-metre line.

 

• A long corner is signalled by the umpire raising one arm straight up.

 

NOTE

 

• Timing (Option 2): Time-related stoppages (like end of quarter) are usually communicated by the timekeeper/scorer, not through this arm signal.

 

• Ball out of play (Option 3): This is generally indicated by pointing the flag/hand in the direction of the restart (free hit, corner, etc.), not by both arms toward the centre.

 

• Bully (Option 4): A bully (used to restart play in specific situations) has its own distinct signal and is not indicated by both arms pointing horizontally to the centre.

question: Who among the following revolutionaries was associated with Swadesh Bandhav Samiti?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashwini Kumar Dutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swadesh Bandhab Samiti was founded by Ashwini Kumar Dutta in 1905 at Barisal (in present-day Bangladesh, then part of Bengal), during the Swadeshi Movement against the Partition of Bengal. (स्वदेश बांधव समिति — अश्विनी कुमार दत्त)

 

• The Samiti worked to promote swadeshi goods, national education, social service and self-reliance among the people, and became a major centre of revolutionary and nationalist activity in East Bengal.

 

• Ashwini Kumar Dutta was a prominent Bengali nationalist leader, educationist and orator, closely associated with the extremist wing of the Indian National Congress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Swadeshi Movement (1905-1911) arose in protest against Lord Curzon's Partition of Bengal (1905) and promoted boycott of British goods and use of indigenous products.

 

• Other prominent leaders of the Swadeshi and revolutionary movement in Bengal included Bipin Chandra Pal, Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Kumar Ghosh.

 

NOTE

 

• Chandrasekhar Azad (Option 1): A key leader of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), active mainly in North India, unrelated to Swadesh Bandhab Samiti.

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 2): A prominent HSRA revolutionary, associated with events like the Lahore Conspiracy Case, not with the Bengal-based Samiti.

 

• Rajguru (Option 3): An HSRA revolutionary who, along with Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev, was involved in the assassination of J.P. Saunders; not linked to Swadesh Bandhab Samiti.

question: Based on Macaulay's Minute, the English Education Act was introduced in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1835.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thomas Babington Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education was presented in 1835, arguing for English as the medium of higher education in India in place of Persian/Sanskrit/Arabic. (मैकाले मिनट — 1835)

 

• Based on this Minute, Governor-General Lord William Bentinck issued the English Education Act, 1835, formally adopting English as the medium of instruction for higher education and government purposes in India.

 

• Macaulay's famous phrase from the Minute — describing the goal of creating "a class of persons, Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals and in intellect" — reflects the Act's intent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Charter Act of 1813 had earlier set aside Rs. 1 lakh annually for education in India, sparking the Orientalist-Anglicist controversy that Macaulay's Minute helped resolve in favour of English education.

 

• Lord William Bentinck was Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835 and is also known for abolishing Sati (1829).

 

NOTE

 

• 1875, 1855, 1815 (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these years correspond to Macaulay's Minute or the English Education Act, which was passed specifically in 1835.

question: Which ministry organized 'Nari Shakti of North East' on the occasion of International Women's Day 2022?
option_1: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
option_3: Ministry of Women and Child Development
option_4: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) organised 'Nari Shakti of North East' on the occasion of International Women's Day 2022 (8 March 2022). (नारी शक्ति ऑफ नॉर्थ ईस्ट — डोनर मंत्रालय)

 

• The event was launched by Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy, who held the DoNER portfolio at the time, to celebrate and showcase the achievements of women entrepreneurs, artisans and change-makers from the North-Eastern states.

 

• DoNER is the nodal ministry responsible for the economic and social development of the eight North-Eastern states of India (the 'Ashta Lakshmi' states).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• International Women's Day is observed globally every year on 8 March.

 

• The Government of India also confers the Nari Shakti Puraskar, the highest civilian award for women, on the same occasion.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Tribal Affairs (Option 2): Deals with the welfare and development of Scheduled Tribes across India, not specifically this North-East event.

 

• Ministry of Women and Child Development (Option 3): The nodal ministry for women's welfare nationally, but 'Nari Shakti of North East' was specifically a DoNER initiative.

 

• Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Option 4): Handles welfare of SCs, OBCs, and other marginalised groups, unrelated to this event.

question: Mrinalini Sarabhai was awarded which of the following awards in 1992?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Bhushan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai (1918-2016) was a renowned Indian classical dancer, choreographer and instructor, trained in Bharatanatyam and Kathakali. (मृणालिनी साराभाई — पद्म भूषण, 1992)

 

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1992 by the Government of India in recognition of her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

• She had earlier received the Padma Shri in 1965 and later founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad, along with her husband, scientist Vikram Sarabhai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai's daughter, Mallika Sarabhai, is also a well-known classical dancer and activist.

 

• The Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, founded in 1949, remains a major centre for Indian classical dance and theatre.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri (Option 1): Mrinalini Sarabhai received this earlier, in 1965, not in 1992.

 

• Kalidas Samman (Option 3): A prestigious award given by the Madhya Pradesh government for classical arts, but not the award conferred on her in 1992.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 4): India's second-highest civilian award; Mrinalini Sarabhai was not conferred this award in 1992.

question: The ________ and _______ determine the corridor for the daily movement in the weighted average call money rate.
option_2: Marginal standing facility, Reverse repo rate
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marginal standing facility, Reverse repo rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) framework, the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and the reverse repo rate together determine the corridor for the daily movement in the weighted average call money rate. (कॉरिडोर — सीमांत स्थायी सुविधा एवं रिवर्स रेपो दर)

 

• The repo rate sits at the centre of this corridor as the RBI's key policy rate; the MSF rate (typically repo + 25 bps) forms the upper bound, while the reverse repo rate (typically repo − 25 bps) forms the lower bound.

 

• This corridor mechanism ensures that short-term interest rates in the money market (specifically the weighted average call money rate) remain anchored close to the policy repo rate, reducing volatility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) was introduced by RBI in 2011 to allow scheduled commercial banks to borrow overnight funds against government securities when interbank liquidity dries up completely.

 

• The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) itself is the overall RBI tool (comprising repo and reverse repo operations) used to manage day-to-day liquidity in the banking system, introduced on the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• Reverse repo, discount rate (Option 1): The 'discount rate' is not part of the standard LAF corridor terminology used by RBI.

 

• Liquidity adjustment facility, repo rate (Option 3): LAF is the overarching framework itself, not one of the two boundary rates of the corridor; repo rate is the centre, not a boundary.

 

• Bank rate, repo rate (Option 4): The bank rate (aligned with the MSF rate) and repo rate are related concepts, but the corridor is specifically defined using the MSF rate and reverse repo rate.

question: Which of the following countries lies in the east of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangladesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bangladesh shares India's eastern land border, surrounded almost entirely by the Indian states of West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, and is conventionally regarded as lying to India's east. (भारत के पूर्व में स्थित देश — बांग्लादेश)

 

• India shares a border of about 4,096 km with Bangladesh — the longest land border India shares with any neighbouring country.

 

• India's neighbours to the east/north-east also include Myanmar, while Bangladesh, among the given options, is the standard answer for a country to India's east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India shares land borders with 7 countries: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan (a small stretch via Pakistan-occupied Kashmir).

 

• India also shares a maritime boundary with Sri Lanka, separated by the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar.

 

NOTE

 

• Sri-Lanka (Option 1): Lies to the south of India, across the Palk Strait, not the east.

 

• Nepal (Option 2): Lies to the north of India, along the Himalayan belt.

 

• Afghanistan (Option 4): Lies to the north-west of India, sharing a border only via Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

question: Which freedom is considered as the 'Hallmark of Democracy'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Freedom of speech and expression.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Freedom of speech and expression, guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution, is widely regarded as the 'Hallmark of Democracy'. (लोकतंत्र की पहचान — भाषण एवं अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता)

 

• It allows citizens to freely express their opinions, criticise the government, and participate meaningfully in the democratic process, making it foundational to a functioning democracy.

 

• The Supreme Court of India has repeatedly held that free speech is the bulwark of a democratic government, essential for the proper functioning of the democratic process.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Freedom of speech and expression is subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2) on grounds such as sovereignty, security of the State, public order, decency, morality, and contempt of court.

 

• Article 19(1) also guarantees other freedoms, including freedom of assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.

 

NOTE

 

• Right against exploitation (Option 1): Covered under Articles 23-24, this prohibits human trafficking, forced labour, and child labour — a distinct fundamental right, not termed the 'hallmark of democracy'.

 

• Right to freedom of religion (Option 2): Covered under Articles 25-28, ensures religious liberty but is not specifically termed the hallmark of democracy.

 

• Freedom of assembly (Option 3): Also under Article 19(1)(b), important for democratic participation, but it is freedom of speech and expression that is specifically called the 'hallmark of democracy'.

question: Which state government has launched the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kaushalya Matritva Yojana was launched by the Chhattisgarh government, under then Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel, to promote institutional pregnancy care and safe motherhood for women during their second pregnancy if the first child was a girl. (कौशल्या मातृत्व योजना — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Under the scheme, eligible women are given a financial incentive of Rs. 5,000 on the birth of a second girl child, to encourage girl-child welfare and safe institutional delivery.

 

• The scheme is named after Mata Kaushalya, the mother of Lord Rama, reflecting Chhattisgarh's cultural association as 'Mata Kaushalya's maternal home' in local tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhattisgarh has also run other welfare schemes such as the Godhan Nyay Yojana (for cattle dung procurement) and Rajiv Gandhi Kisan Nyay Yojana (for farmers).

 

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000 and its capital is Raipur.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Runs its own maternity-benefit schemes like Mamata Yojana, not the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Has separate welfare schemes; the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana is not a Himachal Pradesh scheme.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Runs schemes like the Kerala Social Security Mission; the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana is specific to Chhattisgarh.

question: Who among the following was popularly called the 'Australian Mother of Kathakali'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Louise Lightfoot.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Louise Lightfoot (1902-1979), an Australian dancer and choreographer, is popularly referred to as the 'Australian Mother of Kathakali' for her efforts in promoting and popularising the Indian classical dance form of Kathakali internationally. (ऑस्ट्रेलियाई कथकली माता — लुईस लाइटफुट)

 

• She travelled to India, studied Kathakali, and worked to introduce this Kerala-origin classical dance style to Western audiences, notably taking Kathakali dancer Ram Gopal on international tours.

 

• Her contribution is considered pioneering for building cross-cultural appreciation of Kathakali outside India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup and facial expressions.

 

• Other prominent Indian classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Margot Fonteyn (Option 1): A famous British ballet dancer, unrelated to Kathakali.

 

• Anna Pavlova (Option 2): A celebrated Russian ballet dancer, known for the 'Dying Swan', not associated with Kathakali.

 

• Yelena Andreyanova (Option 3): A 19th-century Russian ballerina, not connected to Kathakali.

question: Xuan Zang and other pilgrims spent time studying in Nalanda, the most famous Buddhist monastery, located in which of the following Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ancient Nalanda Mahavihara, one of the world's oldest and most famous centres of Buddhist learning, is located in the present-day state of Bihar, India. (नालंदा विश्वविद्यालय — बिहार)

 

• The Chinese Buddhist monk-scholar Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) studied and later taught at Nalanda in the 7th century CE, during the reign of King Harshavardhana, and left detailed accounts of its grandeur.

 

• Nalanda flourished as a centre of learning from around the 5th century CE to the 12th century CE, attracting scholars from across Asia, before being destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji's forces around 1193 CE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ruins of Nalanda were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

 

• A modern Nalanda University was re-established near the ancient site in Rajgir, Bihar, as an international institution.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Home to ancient Buddhist sites like Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri, but not Nalanda.

 

• Bengal (Option 2): Had Buddhist centres like Vikramashila's neighbouring regions, but Nalanda itself is not in Bengal.

 

• Sikkim (Option 4): Known for Buddhist monasteries of the Himalayan tradition, but Nalanda is not located there.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the eligibility criteria for being elected as Vice President of India?
option_1: He/She should be a citizen of India.
option_2: He/She should have completed 35 years of age.
option_3: He/She should not hold any office of profit under the Union Government/state government or any subordinate local authority.
option_4: He/She should be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He/She should be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 66 of the Indian Constitution, a person is eligible to be elected Vice-President of India if they are qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) — not the Lok Sabha. (उपराष्ट्रपति पात्रता — राज्यसभा सदस्य के रूप में योग्य)

 

• The other conditions listed are correctly stated: the candidate must be a citizen of India, must have completed 35 years of age, and must not hold any office of profit under the Union or State Government or any local/other authority subject to their control.

 

• Since being 'qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha' is NOT the actual constitutional requirement (it is the requirement for the President, under Article 58), Option 4 is the incorrect statement — making it the answer to this 'NOT correct' question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The President of India, under Article 58, must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha, which is a key distinction from the Vice-President's eligibility.

 

• The Vice-President is elected by members of an Electoral College consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, unlike the President who is elected by a wider Electoral College including state legislatures.

 

NOTE

 

• Citizen of India (Option 1): This is indeed a correct eligibility requirement for the Vice-President under Article 66.

 

• 35 years of age (Option 2): This is also a correct, genuine eligibility requirement for the Vice-President.

 

• No office of profit (Option 3): This is a correctly stated genuine constitutional requirement for Vice-Presidential candidates.

question: Baking soda is ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sodium hydrogencarbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baking soda is the common name for sodium hydrogencarbonate (sodium bicarbonate), with the chemical formula NaHCO₃. (बेकिंग सोडा — सोडियम हाइड्रोजन कार्बोनेट)

 

• It is a mild alkali, widely used in cooking as a leavening agent, since it releases carbon dioxide gas when heated or mixed with an acidic substance, causing dough/batter to rise.

 

• It is prepared industrially by the Solvay process, and is also used in antacids, fire extinguishers, and as a cleaning agent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O), different from baking soda.

 

• When baking soda is heated, it decomposes to form sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.

 

NOTE

 

• Sodium carbonate (Option 1): This is washing soda (Na₂CO₃), a different compound, not baking soda.

 

• Sodium sulphate (Option 2): Chemically Na₂SO₄, used in detergents and glass-making, unrelated to baking soda.

 

• Sodium hydroxide (Option 4): This is caustic soda (NaOH), a strong alkali used in soap-making, not baking soda.

question: Which of the following is NOT 'The Great Lakes' of North America?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Victoria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Great Lakes of North America comprise five interconnected freshwater lakes: Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario. Lake Victoria is NOT among them. (ग्रेट लेक्स — विक्टोरिया झील शामिल नहीं)

 

• Lake Victoria is actually located in East Africa, bordered by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, and is the largest lake in Africa by surface area.

 

• The Great Lakes together form the largest group of freshwater lakes in the world by total area, straddling the border between the United States and Canada.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A common mnemonic for the Great Lakes is 'HOMES' — Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, Superior.

 

• Lake Superior is the largest and deepest of the Great Lakes, and the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

 

NOTE

 

• Superior (Option 1): A genuine member of the Great Lakes of North America.

 

• Huron (Option 2): A genuine member of the Great Lakes of North America.

 

• Erie (Option 3): A genuine member of the Great Lakes of North America.

question:
Which of the following is a plant tissue?

I. Meristematic tissue

II. Permanent tissue
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plant tissues are broadly classified into two main types: Meristematic tissue and Permanent tissue — both statements I and II are correct examples of plant tissue. (पादप ऊतक — विभज्योतक एवं स्थायी ऊतक)

 

• Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing, undifferentiated cells found in regions of growth such as root tips, shoot tips, and cambium (apical, lateral and intercalary meristems).

 

• Permanent tissue is formed when meristematic cells lose the ability to divide and become differentiated for specific functions; it is further classified into simple (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and complex (xylem, phloem) permanent tissues.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots, while phloem transports food (prepared by photosynthesis) throughout the plant.

 

• Parenchyma is the most abundant simple permanent tissue, involved in storage, photosynthesis, and other basic functions.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, as it wrongly excludes meristematic tissue, which is also a genuine plant tissue.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, since both listed tissues are indeed genuine plant tissues.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incorrect, as it wrongly excludes permanent tissue, which is also a genuine plant tissue.

question: In Triple Jump, white flag indicates:
solution_text:
The correct answer is trail is valid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In athletics events like Triple Jump and Long Jump, the officiating judge raises a white flag to indicate that the jump/trial is valid (a fair attempt). (सफ़ेद झंडा — वैध प्रयास)

 

• Conversely, a red flag is raised to indicate a foul or failed trial — for example, when the athlete oversteps the take-off board.

 

• This simple flag-based signalling system allows officials to communicate the validity of a jump instantly to athletes, coaches and spectators.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Triple Jump consists of three phases performed in succession: the hop, the step, and the jump.

 

• India's Eldhose Paul and Abdulla Aboobacker won gold and silver respectively in Triple Jump at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Trail is failure (Option 2): This is indicated by a red flag, not white.

 

• Trail with wind support (Option 3): Wind-assistance is recorded separately via wind gauge readings, not indicated through a white/red flag system.

 

• Allow to trial (Option 4): Permission to begin a trial is typically given by the judge's signal/whistle, not the white flag, which indicates the validity of a completed jump.

question: Which of the following substance has a pH value of about 14?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium hydroxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), commonly known as caustic soda, is a strong alkali with a pH value of about 14, making it one of the most strongly basic common substances. (सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड — pH लगभग 14)

 

• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14: values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral, and values above 7 are basic/alkaline, with 14 representing the strongest common alkalinity.

 

• Strong bases like sodium hydroxide are used in soap-making, paper manufacturing, and as a laboratory reagent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Normal human blood pH is slightly alkaline, around 7.35 to 7.45.

 

• Lemon juice is acidic, with a pH of around 2 to 3, due to citric acid content.

 

NOTE

 

• Blood (Option 1): Has a near-neutral, mildly alkaline pH of about 7.35-7.45, far from 14.

 

• Milk of magnesia (Option 3): A mild base (magnesium hydroxide) with a pH of about 10-11, not as high as 14.

 

• Lemon Juice (Option 4): Is acidic with a pH of about 2-3, the opposite end of the scale from 14.

question: Which of the following folk dances does NOT belong to the state of Mizoram?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Munari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Munari is actually a traditional folk dance of Odisha, not Mizoram, making it the odd one out among the given options. (मुनारी नृत्य — ओडिशा, मिज़ोरम नहीं)

 

• Cheraw (the famous bamboo dance), Chailam, and Zangtalam are all genuine traditional folk dances of Mizoram, performed by the Mizo people during festivals and celebrations.

 

• Cheraw, in particular, is Mizoram's most iconic dance, in which dancers step in and out of criss-crossing bamboo poles that are rhythmically clapped together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Mizoram include Khuallam, Chheihlam, Sarlamkai/Solakia, and Par Lam.

 

• Mizoram's capital is Aizawl, and the state is known for its bamboo-based crafts and dances, reflecting the abundance of bamboo in the region.

 

NOTE

 

• Chailam (Option 2): A genuine traditional folk dance of Mizoram.

 

• Zangtalam (Option 3): A genuine traditional folk dance of Mizoram.

 

• Cheraw (Option 4): Mizoram's most famous and iconic folk (bamboo) dance.

question: Which crop grows best on black soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cotton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Black soil (also known as regur soil or 'black cotton soil') is especially well-suited for growing cotton, due to its high moisture-retention capacity, clay content and richness in minerals like calcium, potassium and magnesium. (काली मिट्टी — कपास की खेती)

 

• Black soil is formed from the weathering of volcanic (Deccan Trap) rocks, and is predominantly found in the Deccan Plateau region, covering states like Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka and parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

 

• The soil's ability to retain moisture for long periods makes it ideal for cotton cultivation even with limited irrigation, earning it the name 'black cotton soil'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Black soil is also suitable for crops like sugarcane, tobacco, wheat, jowar and linseed to some extent.

 

• Maharashtra has the largest area under black soil in India, and is a leading cotton-producing state.

 

NOTE

 

• Coffee (Option 2): Grows best in lateritic soils of hilly regions like Karnataka's Western Ghats (Coorg), not black soil.

 

• Maize (Option 3): Grows well in a variety of soils, especially well-drained alluvial soils, not specifically identified with black soil.

 

• Millets (Option 4): Typically grown in less fertile, sandy or loamy soils in dry regions, not primarily associated with black soil.

question: Who has been appointed as Secretary to President Droupadi Murmu in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajesh Verma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajesh Verma, a 1987-batch IAS officer, was appointed as Secretary to President Droupadi Murmu in August 2022. (राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मू के सचिव — राजेश वर्मा)

 

• Prior to this appointment, Rajesh Verma served as Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

 

• Droupadi Murmu took office as the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022, becoming the first tribal woman and second woman to hold the office.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Droupadi Murmu previously served as the Governor of Jharkhand (2015-2021), and before that as a minister in Odisha.

 

• The President's Secretariat handles the day-to-day administrative work of the Rashtrapati Bhavan.

 

NOTE

 

• Ranjit Rath (Option 1): Served as Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of Oil India Limited, not Secretary to the President.

 

• Suresh N Patel (Option 3): A former Director General of the Border Security Force (BSF), not the President's Secretary.

 

• Santosh Iyer (Option 4): Known as an automobile industry executive (Mercedes-Benz India), unrelated to this appointment.

question: Identify the freedom fighter who, as a child, hated going to school and found it suffocating and oppressive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore, as a child, deeply disliked the rigid, rote-learning-based formal schooling of his time, finding it suffocating and oppressive, and he wrote about this discomfort in his memoirs. (रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर — बचपन में विद्यालय से नफ़रत)

 

• This dislike of conventional schooling later inspired him to found Shantiniketan (and subsequently Visva-Bharati University) in 1901/1921, based on a more natural, open-air, holistic style of education close to nature.

 

• Tagore became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913), for his collection of poems Gitanjali.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tagore also composed the national anthems of both India ('Jana Gana Mana') and Bangladesh ('Amar Shonar Bangla').

 

• Visva-Bharati University, founded by Tagore, was later declared an Institution of National Importance.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 1): While Gandhi had his own views on education (e.g., Nai Talim), he is not specifically remembered for hating school as a child in the way described here.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 2): Was largely educated at home by tutors before going to Harrow and Cambridge; not associated with this particular childhood characterization.

 

• Jyotiba Phule (Option 3): A pioneering social reformer and educationist, but not specifically remembered for hating school as a child in this manner.

question: Choose the correct pair from the following options.
option_4: Seventh Five-Year Plan - PV Narasimha Rao
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth Five-Year Plan - Indira Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979) was implemented during the tenure of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, focusing on the objectives of 'removal of poverty' (Garibi Hatao) and attainment of self-reliance. (पंचवर्षीय योजना — पांचवीं योजना, इंदिरा गांधी)

 

• India's Five-Year Plans were formulated by the Planning Commission, and each plan is associated with the Prime Minister(s) in office during its implementation period.

 

• The Fifth Plan was terminated one year early, in 1978, by the Janata Party government which came to power after the Emergency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015, ending the era of formal Five-Year Plans after the Twelfth Plan (2012-2017).

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) was launched during Jawaharlal Nehru's tenure, focusing on agriculture.

 

NOTE

 

• Sixth Five-Year Plan - Rajiv Gandhi (Option 1): Incorrect; the Sixth Plan (1980-1985) was implemented under Indira Gandhi, not Rajiv Gandhi.

 

• Fourth Five-Year Plan - Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 3): Incorrect; the Fourth Plan (1969-1974) was implemented under Indira Gandhi — Nehru had died in 1964, well before this plan began.

 

• Seventh Five-Year Plan - PV Narasimha Rao (Option 4): Incorrect; the Seventh Plan (1985-1990) was implemented under Rajiv Gandhi; PV Narasimha Rao's tenure (1991-1996) came after a plan holiday, overseeing economic liberalisation and roughly aligning with the Eighth Plan period.
